## Objective
- Add a realistic pit lane and 10 physical team garages to the existing track-drawing racing game.
- Call the player to pit halfway through the race, including at lap 2 for a 4-lap race or lap 5 for a 10-lap race.

## Requirements
- Pit entry should branch from the track before the start/finish point; pit exit should rejoin after it.
- Garages should be physical, and the player should stop at their pit box.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Explored the project structure and inspected race, track, car, and world code.

### Active
- Implement the pit lane, garages, and halfway pit-stop gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect race initialization, lap progression, and render/update loops in `src/main.js`, plus world construction in `src/world.js`.
2. Add pit lane geometry and 10 garages near the start/finish section, with a usable player pit box.
3. Add a midpoint pit call and stopping/service state; test across race lengths.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: race initialization, progression, HUD, and update logic.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js race-world geometry and scene construction.
- `src/track.js`: track samples and distance-based track positions.
- `src/car.js`: player and AI car construction.
- `index.html`: race interface markup.
- `styles.css`: game and HUD styling.

## Important Context
- No files have been changed yet.
- The game is a browser-based Three.js racing game with a user-drawn track and configurable race laps.

## Objective
- Add a realistic pit lane and 10 physical team garages to the track-drawing racing game.

## Requirements
- Pit entry branches from the track before the start/finish point; pit exit rejoins after it.
- Garages must be physical, and the player must stop at their pit box.
- Pit call occurs halfway through the race: lap 2 of 4 or lap 5 of 10.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions; briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Place the pit lane on one side of the start/finish area, with the player’s box near the start/finish line.
- Use 10 distinct team garage structures and markings.

### Completed
- Added pit-lane geometry, edge lines, 10 distinct physical garage structures, and a marked player pit box in `src/world.js`; exposed `pitRoute` and `playerPitBox`.
- Added halfway pit-call timing and initialized/reset pit-stop state in `src/main.js`.
- Added pit route steering and speed demands, route advancement, a stationary service phase, and pit-exit transition in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Integrate pit phases with `updatePlayerProgress()` so pit travel does not miscount checkpoints or laps and progress resumes correctly at exit.
- Review collision, recovery, and race-finish behavior during pit phases.
- Add pit-call/status HUD feedback.
- Verify lane continuity and test both 4- and 10-lap race timing and pit stops.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Update `updatePlayerProgress()` to bypass normal checkpoint/lap processing during pit travel and correctly resume track progress after rejoining.
2. Review pit physics and phase transitions, including collisions, recovery, missed/overshot pit boxes, and race finish.
3. Add pit status feedback, then run available checks and verify both race lengths.

- `src/main.js`: Pit state and physics, player progress/lap handling, HUD, collisions, recovery, and race update loop.

- `index.html`: Race HUD markup.
- `styles.css`: HUD and race-message styling.

- No checks or race-play verification have been run.

## Objective
- Add a realistic pit lane with 10 physical team garages and require the player to stop at their pit box after a halfway race call.

## Requirements
- Pit entry branches before the start/finish point; pit exit rejoins after it.
- Call the stop halfway: lap 2 of 4 or lap 5 of 10.
- Garages must be physical; the player must stop at their pit box.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Place the pit lane beside the start/finish area, with the player’s box near the start/finish line.
- Use 10 distinct team garage structures and markings.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added pit-lane geometry and route, 10 garage structures, marked player pit box, halfway pit call, automated pit driving, service, and pit-exit transitions.
- Added pit progress/lap counting, checkpoint pausing, collision suppression, disabled recovery during pit travel, and pit status HUD styling/state.
- `npm ci` succeeded; desktop and mobile preview screenshots were captured.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify race progress, checkpoint/lap state, finish behavior, pit-box arrival, lane continuity, and HUD through pit entry and exit for 4- and 10-lap races.

### Blocked
- No automated test suite is configured (`npm test` exits with `Error: no test specified`); browser interaction testing has not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Use the browser preview to exercise pit flow and lap/checkpoint state in 4- and 10-lap races.
2. Check pit-box arrival, pit-lane continuity, and HUD presentation.
3. Run available checks and briefly report assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Pit state, physics, progress/checkpoint handling, collision and recovery logic, HUD, race update loop.
- `src/world.js`: Pit lane route, garages, pit box, and race-world construction.
- `index.html`: Race HUD markup.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD and pit status styling.

## Important Context
- Pit route starts at `track.length - 190`, spans 380 m, and ends at 190 m; the player box is about 190 m into the route.
- `callAfterLaps = Math.floor(totalLaps / 2) - 1` triggers the call as lap 2 of 4 or lap 5 of 10 begins.
- `advancePitRoute()` updates `p.progressDist`; pit-route timing-line crossings call `completeLap()`.
- Pit phases are `waiting`, `called`, `driving-in`, `servicing`, and `driving-out`.
- Preview captures: `/tmp/opencode/pit-captures/final-desktop.png` and `/tmp/opencode/pit-captures/final-mobile.png`.
- Changes are uncommitted.
